replication.target_description: EmpaToM accuracy, age-group main effect in mixed ANOVA across ToM and factual reasoning questions; independent younger/older sample tested in MRI scanner.

n.quote: The final sample comprised 42 younger (21 females, age range = 18–30, M = 24.00, s.d. = 3.20) and 44 older (22 females, age range = 65–77, M = 69.50, s.d. = 3.74) individuals.
n.sample_role: participants in the target test; younger and older adult groups
n.exclusions: 15 of 101 excluded: inability to undergo scanning (5), hearing/sight problems (4), termination/technical problems (2), neurological abnormalities (4). Two below-chance participants retained. Button-box and sleep trials excluded and scores proportionally adjusted.

reported_success.quote: Concerning ToM we replicated the effect of age on ToM accuracy

notes: Broad locator does not uniquely identify ANOVA term or accuracy versus reaction time. Selected age-group main effect on accuracy because target concerns age-group differences; this test includes factual reasoning control trials, not isolated ToM accuracy. Alternative printed accuracy interactions: original partial η² = 0.28, p < 0.001, F(1,105) = 41.21; replication partial η² = 0.240, p < 0.001, F1,84 = 26.580. Authors separately state they did not replicate ToM reaction-time age effect; successful verdict here is specific to accuracy. No metric conversion. Exact test selection is not uniquely established by the broad supplied locator, so target_match is null for both sides despite locating the matching paper, sample, and outcome family.
